items.stem: What is the single most important precaution when handling internal PC components?

options.text: Guard against electrostatic discharge by grounding yourself and handling boards by the edges
options.rationale: Correct: ESD can silently damage components, so grounding and edge-handling are essential.

options.text: Work as quickly as possible to reduce exposure
options.rationale: Speed does not protect components; ESD control does.

options.text: Keep the power supply switched on for convenience
options.rationale: Live power while building risks shorts and shocks.

options.text: Hold chips firmly by their gold contacts
options.rationale: Touching contacts risks ESD damage and contamination.

items.explanation: Correct: ESD can silently damage components, so grounding and edge-handling are essential.

items.stem: Which TWO symptoms most directly point to a memory (RAM) fault during bring-up? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The system fails POST with a memory-specific beep or LED code
options.rationale: Correct: POST codes flag memory faults explicitly.

options.text: Random crashes or memory errors that follow a specific stick when swapped
options.rationale: Correct: a fault that tracks one stick indicates that module.
A wallpaper change is cosmetic and unrelated to RAM.

options.text: The keyboard LEDs are the wrong colour
options.rationale: Keyboard lighting is unrelated to a RAM fault.

items.explanation: Correct: POST codes flag memory faults explicitly.

items.stem: A PC powers on but gives no display. Following a structured method, what should you check first?

options.text: The simplest causes first: power connections, monitor input and reseating the GPU/RAM
options.rationale: Correct: structured troubleshooting checks the simplest, most likely causes first.
Replacing parts before diagnosis is wasteful and premature.
No display at POST is a hardware-stage issue, not an OS one.

options.text: Update the GPU driver from within the OS
options.rationale: You cannot reach the OS if there is no display at boot.

items.explanation: Correct: structured troubleshooting checks the simplest, most likely causes first.
